CONVENTION '86

while most of the nation was suffering
through the dog days of August, more than one
hundred Psi Upsilon undergraduates and alum
ni were rolling up their sleeves and tackling the
business of the Fraternity. The event was, of
course, the 143rd Convention, held under the

auspices of the Theta Theta Chapter at the Uni
versity of Washington.

Delegates spent August 20 through August
24 attending legislative meetings, workshops,
seminars, and committee meetings, all of which
helped give them a better knowledge of how
Psi U operiates. Business meetings were inter
spersed with some dynamic presentations and
highly effective speakers, including William P.
Gerberding, President of the University of
Washington; Dr. Robert H. Shaffer, Dean
Emeritus Indiana University; Brewster
at

Denny, Professor of Public Affairs at UW and
a member of the
"founding family" of Seattle;
John B. Fery, Theta Theta '52, Chairman of the
Board and Chief Executive Officer of Boise Cas
cade; and James A. Swanke, Jr., Rho '80, na
tionally recognized expert in the field of risk
management, which was the major focus of this
Convention.

Official business was not the only item on the
agenda, though, and delegates found oppor
tunities to enjoy Seattle's hospitality and the
best weather of the summer. Some arrived early
or stayed late in order to include an excursion

to the International Expo just two hours away
in Vancouver, British Columbia. Others found
time to visit the natural wonders of both Mount
Rainier and Olympic National Park. Hopefully
everyone explored the major attractions in Se
attle, where shoppers, sightseers, and sports
men could find a multitude of diversions in this

magnificent city rising from the Puget Sound.

of PSI UPSILON 11

The Convention itself afforded an
opportu
nity to partake of Seattle's breathtaking beauty
during the Emerald City Cruise. Brothers and
guests boarded the "Spirit of '76" for a threehour trip through the Puget Sound and the
adjoining lakes, Washington and Union. The
fraternal experience was heightened by a set
ting which was truly spectacular.

Most memorable of all, perhaps, were the
brothers met, friends made, and stories ex
changed (some true!). The annual Convention
is one of the few times when it is
possible to
gauge the true scope of Psi Upsilon. With most
Chapters represented, there was the oppor
tunity to see the Fraternity as a whole, span
ning the continent and her finest academic in
stitutions. Brothers from every part of North
America, from the class of 1923 to the class of
1990, were joined by a common bond.

It would be impossible to discuss the 143rd
Convention without recognizing some impor
tant contributors to its success. At the top of
this list are Richard Cuff '87, undergraduate
president of the Theta Theta; Bill Borkowski,
Theta Theta '88; and Glen Hubbard, Theta
Theta '88. Strong assists go to the entire un
dergraduate membership of the Theta Theta,
who worked tirelessly to make this Convention
the success that it was.

Delegates departed the Pacific Northwest
weary but fulfilled. While in Seattle, they dis
cussed, debated, argued, learned, shared, and
grew. They left with a renewed enthusiasm for
Psi Upsilon and a heightened anticipation of
the 144th Convention in New York City!

Dear Brothers:
It is with great pleasure and pride that we present this report of
the success of the 1985-86 Annual Giving program. A new high of
$145,123 in gifts ($3,618 more than last year) was achieved through
the generous contributions of 2,213 loyal alumni. This represents an
average gift of $65.58, certainly one of the highest averages in the
fraternity world.
Once again the alumni of Psi Upsilon have set new records in
giving, thereby enabling us to extend the warm hand of brotherhood
to yet another generation of fine undergraduates. This enthusiastic

response is truly heartwarming, and the Executive Council extends
its heartiest and most sincere thanks for each measure of assistance,

large and small.
The following record of statistics and lists, which represents gifts
received from July 1, 1985 through June 30, 1986 (gifts received
subsequent to June 30 have been credited to the 1986-87 program),
serves to honor the faithful and supportive members of Psi Upsilon

who, by their generosity, have enabled the Fraternity to move
forward on its distinguished course.
This year we have initiated a new concept of recognizing the suin
total of contributions which an alumnus has made to the Annual
Giving program since its inception in 1964. New levels of support
have been named, borrowing from some of our great Psi U songs, to
acknowledge each alumnus' cumulative giving record to the
Fraternity. Names in bolder print represent leadership contributors
(1985-86 gift of $50 or more), and years of consecutive giving are
shown in parentheses after the name and class of donors.
As we chart the course for the future, we must ask our alumni to
raise their sights still further, so that we can maintain and even

expand the scope of Psi Upsilon's services and activities in behalf of
our undergraduate Chapters. The 1986-87 budget calls for $156,800

in Annual Giving contributions. Of great encouragement is the fact
that this year's program is off to a resounding start. We beUeve that
the alumni of Psi Upsilon again will rise to the challenge of meeting,
perhaps even exceeding, this ambitious goal!
Yours in the Bonds,
